rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In praise constructions, the accusative after نعم is analyzed like the accusative after حسبك به or ويحه, with comparable praise force.
rows.anchor: هذا الباب فإنه ينتصب كانتصاب ما انتصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concealed element placed before its explanation in this construction cannot stand alone: it requires a later interpreter and cannot be replaced by an overt noun.
rows.anchor: وإنما هو إضمار مقدم قبل الاسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In نعم الرجل عبد الله, نعم governs الرجل rather than عبد الله; reversing the order gives a separate clause identifying what عبد الله is like.
rows.anchor: عمل نعم في الرجل ولم يعمل في عبد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نعم can govern a hidden element explained afterward, or can govern an overt noun directly; the two patterns parallel ويحه and ربه.
rows.anchor: ثم يعملان في الذي فسر المضمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person identified after نعم الرجل must be the same person denoted by الرجل; عبد الله نعم الرجل cannot mean the man is someone else.
rows.anchor: عبد الله نعم الرجل والرجل غير عبد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الرجل after نعم names a praiseworthy class: the speaker places the individual among a whole group of good people rather than identifying a particular man by his quality.
rows.anchor: من أمة كلهم صالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A plural group cannot be praised by splitting its members as نعم صغارهم وكبارهم; acceptable forms name the classes or praise the group as a whole.
rows.anchor: إلا أن تقول قومك نعم الصغار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When نعم governs an overt noun, that noun is definite or annexed, as in الرجل or غلام الرجل, while referring to a class rather than a specific individual.
rows.anchor: غلام الرجل إذا لم ترد شيئا بعينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نعم may be masculine or feminine: نعمت المرأة is more frequent, though نعم المرأة is also said.
rows.anchor: والحذف في نعمت أكثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural subject marker is not shown after نعم; speakers rely on its following explanation, and frequent use fixes this deletion as with بئس.
rows.anchor: يكتفون بالذي يفسره كما قالوا مررت بكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نعم and بئس derive from نعم and بئس and function as verbs only for praise and blame, respectively.
rows.anchor: ولا يكون منهما فعل لغير هذا المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In هذه الدار نعمت البلد, the feminine marker follows البلد understood as الدار; when البلد is masculine, نعم البلد is also used.
rows.anchor: لما كان البلد الدار أقحموا التاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poet uses masculine فيه with الدار because the house is construed as a place, showing agreement can follow that sense.
rows.anchor: فقال فيه لأن الدار مكان فحمله على ذلك

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil analyzes حبذا as a single unit like حب الشيء; ذا remains masculine because the compound has become a fixed idiom.
rows.anchor: وزعم الخليل رحمه الله أن حبذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أيما can modify an indefinite, serve as a circumstantial qualifier with a definite, or function interrogatively; it does not mark number or introduce an exception.
rows.anchor: لا تكون لتبيين العدد ولا في الاستثناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أيما فتى is interrogative, with an element of astonishment, as shown by the comparable questions سبحان الله من هو وما هو.
rows.anchor: فهذا استفهام فيه معنى التعجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أحد and the listed words occur under negation, not as affirmative predicates, circumstantials, exceptions, or classifiers that specify a type or number.
rows.anchor: في النفى مبنيا عليهن ومبنية على غيرهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After عسل ملء جرة or دين شعر كلبين, رفع is the normal analysis because the following noun is an adjective; نصب is also possible after a complete clause.
rows.anchor: فإذا قلت له عسل ملء جرة وعليه دين شعر كلبين فالوجه الرفع لأنه وصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In عليها مثلها زبد, زبد may be a بدل or an answer equivalent to هو زبد, but it is not an adjective because it is a noun.
rows.anchor: فإذا قلت عليها مثلها زبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The numeral phrase ثلاثة وثلاثين is one vocative unit, not two independently addressed nouns; like ثلاثة عشر, it therefore takes accusative form.
rows.anchor: وإن لم تندب قلت يا ثلاثة وثلاثين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A phrase such as يا ضاربا رجلا is definite in address, but tanwin remains because the noun phrase is not complete until رجلا.
rows.anchor: ورجلا من تمام الاسم فصار التنوين بمنزلة حرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tanwin also remains in يا خيرا منك because the final word is not the end of the addressed name; deletion applies only at the name's end.
rows.anchor: لو سميت رجلا خيرا منك لقلت يا خيرا منك فألزمته التنوين وهو معرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dropping tanwin for lightness does not change the intended tanwin meaning, just as deletion does not alter the agent in ضاربك قاعدا.
rows.anchor: لأن الرجل لا يجعل ضاربا نكرة إذا أردت معنى التنوين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In يا أخا رجل, أخا is indefinite because it is annexed to an indefinite; رجل is not a vocative here and cannot be treated as a silently definite noun.
rows.anchor: فلا يكون الأخ هاهنا إلا نكرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In لا رجل اليوم ظريفا and لا رجل فيها عاقلا, the adjective is tanwinned when a word intervenes; noun and adjective cannot be treated as one word across that separation.
rows.anchor: وذلك قولك لا رجل اليوم ظريفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An annexed noun such as ماء سماء is not compounded with what follows like خمسة عشر, so its adjective follows the usual pattern and remains tanwinned.
rows.anchor: لا ماء سماء لك باردا ولا مثله عاقلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When tanwin is removed because of annexation, the adjective follows the ordinary annexed construction, as in لا ضاربا زيدا لك and لا حسنا وجه الأخ فيها.
rows.anchor: فإذا كففت التنوين وأضفت كان بمنزلته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After لا ماء ولا لبن, the adjective for لبن may be tanwinned or not; if it describes ماء it must be tanwinned because the paired words form one unit needing a predicate.
rows.anchor: فإن جعلت الصفة للماء لم يكن الوصف إلا منونا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In لا أبا لك, an omitted locative element is understood.
rows.anchor: لك فها ~~هنا إضمار مكان

rows.speaker: أهل الحجاز
rows.claim: The Hijazis answer من زيدا? with the questioned accusative form, repeating the case used in the question as quotation.
rows.anchor: اعلم أن أهل الحجاز يقولون إذا قال الرجل رأيت زيدا من زيدا

rows.speaker: بنو تميم
rows.claim: Tamim speakers answer in the nominative in every case; Sībawayh says this is more analogical than the Hijazi quotation.
rows.anchor: بنو تميم فيرفعون على كل حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hijazi quotation is allowed for a dominant proper name because it is the most-used identifying name; it is not extended to ordinary names, and a kunya behaves like a name.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز في غير الاسم الغالب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For رأيت أخا خالد, the expected answer is nominative because the name is not dominant; accusative is possible only by the quoted-name pattern.
rows.anchor: والوجه الرفع لأنه ليس باسم غالب

rows.speaker: يونس
rows.claim: Yunus returns coordinated names to the nominative by analogy and treats زيد بن عمرو as one name, quoting the compound without tanwin; a separate adjective such as الطويل is raised.
rows.anchor: وسألت يونس عن ~~رأيت زيد بن عمرو فقال أقول من زيد ابن عمرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some speakers extend quotation across coordinated words; Sībawayh accepts the form, but when من separates the second phrase, أخو زيد is raised as an independent answer.
rows.anchor: تبا له وويلا وتبا له وويل له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a conjunction is added before من, the response after it must be nominative; only من itself regularly permits quotation.
rows.anchor: لم يكن فيما بعده إلا الرفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tanwin is normally retained before a descriptive or annexed second name; it is omitted only when the combination has become a dominant identifying name such as ابن الزبير.
rows.anchor: وذلك قولك هذا زيد ابن أخيك

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil keeps tanwin in زيد ابن زيدك: Zayd is made definite by the attached pronoun, not by becoming a dominant compound name; Yunus omits tanwin.
rows.anchor: فقال الخليل هذا زيد ابن زيدك

rows.speaker: يونس
rows.claim: Yunus does not pronounce tanwin in زيد ابن زيدك, differing from al-Khalil's preferred analogical analysis.
rows.anchor: وأما يونس فلا ينون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If ابن is an apposition or repetition rather than an adjective, tanwin remains; an ordinary name like أخو زيد also keeps tanwin before ابن عمرو.
rows.anchor: ولكنك تجعله بدلا أو تكريرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form بني عمرو is attributed to Abu Amr and Yunus to avoid two adjacent sukuns, but the regular rule remains unless broader Arabic usage establishes an exception.
rows.anchor: وليس بالكثير في الكلام ككثرة ابن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These accusative verbal nouns emphasize an already stated action or assertion; the construction is neither an adjective nor an object governed by a preceding noun, and it uses an understood verb.
rows.anchor: كأنه قال أحق حقا فجعله بدلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tanwin or an indefinite verbal noun can reinforce an earlier assertion: عرفا follows an acknowledgment, while the poet's قسما reinforces an oath, like سيرا after سير عليه.
rows.anchor: له على ألف درهم عرفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Emphatic verbal nouns may take the definite article or annexation, as in صنع الله, وعد الله, and خلقه; these forms work like the other verbal nouns in this construction.
rows.anchor: وكذلك الإضافة بمنزلة الألف واللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the prohibition sequence beginning in 4:23, Sībawayh reads كتاب الله as an emphatic verbal noun: the rulings are written and binding on the audience.
rows.anchor: أيمانكم كتاب الله عليكم @QE@

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some grammarians instead parse كتاب الله as governed by عليكم; Sībawayh's explanation treats it as emphasis.
rows.anchor: أيمانكم كتاب الله عليكم @QE@

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: One reported analysis makes صبغة الله an accusative governed by an imperative understood from the context.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم @QB@ صبغة الله @QE@

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another reported analysis treats صبغة الله as emphasis rather than an imperative object.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم لا بل توكيدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A nominative reading is also possible by supplying an implied noun, as in ذاك وعد الله, or an implied copula, as in هو دعوة الحق.
rows.anchor: على أن يضمر شيئا هو المظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In دعوة الحق, the annexed verbal noun reiterates that the preceding expression الله أكبر is a true invocation.
rows.anchor: دعاء الحق ولكنه توكيد كأنه قال دعاء حقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing بلاغ is likewise an emphatic source noun, understood as ذاك بلاغ.
rows.anchor: كأنه قال ذاك بلاغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the shepherd's poem, وجيف المطايا emphasizes the earlier implied verb أوجفت, continuing the same pattern of an omitted verb replaced by its verbal noun.
rows.anchor: فجعل وجيف المطايا توكيدا لأوجفت الذى هو فى ضميره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite predicate in ما كان أحد مثلك or خيرا منك is informative under broad negation: it denies anyone equal to or exceeding the person addressed.
rows.anchor: أن يكون في مثل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An affirmative كان رجل ذاهبا is uninformative, while adding a specific lineage in كان رجل من آل فلان فارسا can convey new information.
rows.anchor: أن ذلك في آل فلان وقد يجهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أحد is used for general negation; ما أتاك رجل can deny a particular count, gender, or strength, whereas ما أتاك أحد denies all such possibilities.
rows.anchor: فإذا قال ما أتاك أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With an established locative predicate, the adjective follows the name in nominative; when the locative is syntactically canceled, the adjective is accusative, and both orders are attested.
rows.anchor: وتقول ما كان فيها أحد خير منك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A required locative is better placed early, while an optional, canceled locative is better delayed; Sībawayh compares this ordering to أظن and أحسب.
rows.anchor: إذا أردت الإلغاء فكلما أخرت الذي تلغيه كان أحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quranic order ولم يكن له كفوا أحد places the optional locative between the predicate and subject; some Bedouins instead say ولم يكن كفوا أحد.
rows.anchor: كأنهم أخروها حيث كانت غير مستقرة
